comparison.objective: Align moulding in a mitre box, saw through it at 45°, then stow the saw and workpiece; candidate commissions a compact shock absorber.
comparison.physical_skill: PR requires bimanual workpiece fixturing, saw-slot alignment, and repeated constrained reciprocation. Candidate requires small hex-tool engagement, counterholding, fine rotary tuning, locking torque, and iterative guarded cycling.
comparison.success_condition: PR requires an on-mark 45° through-cut, saw returned, moulding removed, and arms reset; partial credit tracks placement and kerf/strokes. Candidate requires two acceptable dynamic stops and lock-retention verification.
comparison.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization and repeated motion, but the functional abilities are materially different: guided cutting versus tuning and securing a dynamic energy absorber. Candidate overload, rebound, and drift thresholds are not quantified.
